Lessons.Title: Symmetry in Action (optional)
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will the purpose of this optional lesson is for you to practice visualizing and drawing figures given lines of symmetry and to use symmetry to solve problems about side lengths and perimeter.
In this lesson, you continue to work with line-symmetric figures in the context of paper folding. You are given the result of folding paper along your lines of symmetry and reason about the original figure and its perimeter. As you think about the lengths of segments in line-symmetric shapes and find perimeters, you practice looking for and making use of structure (MP7).

2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up: Which One Doesn’t Belong: Figures (10 minutes); Activity 1: Before and After (15 minutes); Activity 2: Before and After, Perimeter Edition (20 minutes); Cool-down: Fold It Once (5 minutes)
Source-goal geometric reasoning: Use a fold symmetry axis to reconstruct the whole shape, then calculate original side lengths and perimeter—not the folded outline.

Edulytics worked explanation: Identify the original fold line and the partial outline from the source task. Reflect the folded part to reconstruct the whole figure. Use reconstructed lengths for its complete boundary; count a shared fold only when it is on the original exterior. A 9-by-6-cm rectangle has original perimeter 2 × (9 + 6) = 30 cm.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (not gated original): A 9-by-6-cm rectangular paper is folded on its symmetry line. Find its original perimeter.
Original student diagrams, teacher card sorting, paper folding, and physical drawings require figure-by-figure / teacher validation.
